title: Decision Value of Uptake Data for Encouragement Policies under Weak Compliance
banked_reason: D0.5: strict full-cell versus outcome-only regret separation and its 0.267/0.2689966005 certificate and open-neighborhood transfer are not delivered; achieved incremental below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The promised strict full-cell versus outcome-only regret separation (including the 0.267/0.2689966005 certificate and open-neighborhood transfer) is not delivered: the core instead proves only weak projection dominance, an outcome-only rate bracket, and a 3/2 full-cell envelope, leaving the headline information frontier open.

The lawful all-rule lower bound and outcome-only n^{-1/2} rate are substantive but specialized companion results, while the note’s motivating information-gap theorem and supporting computational certificate remain open.
proof_attempt_summary: Four D0 solve rounds and twelve directives established lawful centered paths, an outcome-only rate bracket, a uniform bounded-Lipschitz full-cell Gaussian limit, and exact weak information ordering. The proposed strict regret gap was not proved: the lower certificate reaches only C0≈0.166, the full-cell bound is 3/2, and no complete interval certificate or selector/deficiency transfer was produced. D0.5 passed mathematical and cited-source checks but graded the delivered result incremental, below the field floor.
tldr: Outcome arm means identify encouragement welfare, but retaining uptake has not yet been shown to have strict decision value.  In the two-stratum weak-compliance design, a lawful centered three-point prior gives the exact outcome-only lower constant \(C_0=(3/4)\Phi(-15/(8\sqrt6))>27/200\) for every fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1/40]\), while the rule that always chooses no invitation bounds outcome-only normalized minimax regret by \(3/4\).  Hence outcome-only minimax causal welfare regret is \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\).  A separate fixed-nuisance construction gives a positive lower constant at \(\epsilon=0\).  The explicit profiled full-cell rule is uniformly bounded by \(3/2\) over the broad interior class and does not know \(h\).  Deleting uptake is an exact parameter-independent projection, so full observations weakly Blackwell-dominate outcome-only observations at every finite sample size; strictness remains open.
gap: Published encouragement-policy work identifies welfare and gives regular regret rates, while weak-instrument and local treatment-choice work supplies separate asymptotic tools. None of the inspected papers determines whether the outcome-only experiment is decision-sufficient when compliance is of order \(n^{-1/2}\), or gives a strict risk comparison with joint uptake--outcome cells.
fill: The paper constructs the full and coarsened local experiments from the observable coordinates \((\Delta_{n,j},\widehat\gamma_j)\), gives a mixed-rate Gaussian sequence with the nuisance covariance and cross-covariance blocks shown explicitly, certifies one \(h\)-independent plug-in cell score over the complete parameter box, proves an all-rule outcome-only lower bound from a lawful centered three-point prior, and transfers both statements with parameter-independent kernels, an exact bounded-loss deficiency inequality, and a uniform action-stability bound.
